\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]\footnotesize
\item Both predictors are effectively tie-free over the held-out rows (19,794 and 20,437
distinct values respectively; largest tie block 0.03\%), so the Spearman comparison
is like-for-like on the criterion of \S\ref{sec:ties} and $\tau_b$ \citep{kendall1945}
is expected to agree with it in direction. It does, and by a larger margin.
\item The advantage appears in \emph{both} detection and quantification rather than only
in the zero block. Liu is the weakest partition on every metric, and its AUROC interval
spans zero.
\item Intervals are protospacer-clustered bootstraps over 2,000 resamples. Reproduce
with \path{revision/task_1_3_tie_robust.py}.
\end{tablenotes}
